source.title: From Narrow Unlearning to Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Erum Mushtaq; Anil Ramakrishna; Satyapriya Krishna; Sattvik Sahai; P. Goyal; Kai-Wei Chang; Tao Zhang; Rahul Gupta

record.tranche_reason: The study measures overlap between RAI concept representations and refusal changes after unlearning, but it does not measure neuron polysemanticity or test any listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The refusal-score experiments concern cross-domain refusal changes, not polysemantic neurons. The representation analysis measures concept-vector similarity, a related but different construct; its findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Refusal-score and MMLU results are not rows because they do not measure the claim's subject.
record.test_reason: The study is about emergent misalignment from refusal unlearning in Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B. It never measures individual neurons, polysemanticity, superposition or explanation scoring, so its results bear on no version of the claim. Its only internal analysis is concept-vector (PCA direction) cosine similarity at layer 5, a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version. 'cites_only' overstates even the citation link: the paper does not cite the original sources. Neither 'discusses' nor 'cites_only' fits strictly; T6 (neither tests nor uses) is the operative call.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors conclude that narrow refusal unlearning (NPO) reduces refusals on the target concept but also produces emergent misalignment in other RAI domains, with safety interventions affecting more domains. Adding cross-entropy on retain sets largely, though not always fully, restores refusals. Concept overlap at the representation level correlates with the extent of emergent misalignment. The overlap analysis is reported only for Mistral.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses refusal unlearning and concept-vector similarity analysis; it does not use the original neuron-visualization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that LoRA-based unlearning was insufficient for the Qwen safety setting, so it used full-model training there; results also vary by intervention concept and model.

fits_no_version.finding: In Mistral-7B-0.3v at layer 5, the cybersecurity concept vector is more similar to safety samples, while the safety concept vector overlaps broadly with all other RAI concepts. This pattern matches the observed spread of emergent misalignment after unlearning: cybersecurity interventions mainly hit safety, and safety interventions hit nearly all other concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overlap between RAI concepts at the representation level (concept-vector similarity) is associated with cross-domain refusal loss after narrow refusal unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study does not provide uncertainty estimates for the reported results. Its representation analysis uses a training-free concept-vector method, one stated layer, and the paper reports the overlap result for Mistral; the authors also note that they did not evaluate larger-scale models.
record.rows_left_out: Refusal-score and MMLU results in Tables 2–4 were left out because they do not measure polysemanticity or a listed version of the claim.

All: no examination of how polysemantic neurons arise.

All: no neuron explanation scoring or activation-range analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The study is irrelevant to the polysemantic_neurons phenomenon; it was likely retrieved because of the 'concept entanglement' wording. The reader's relation 'discusses' is too generous: the paper never mentions polysemanticity or neurons. Leaving out the refusal-score and MMLU tables was correct.
